summary: Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who earned his doctorate (~1949–1955) and completed his Habilitation (~1959–1964) at the University of Hamburg, studying under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring. He served as Ordinarius für Indische Philologie at the Free University of Berlin (1966–1991).

Klaus Butzenberger worked in Indology, philosophy, and Tibetology, studying at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm. He taught at Munich, the Free University of Berlin, and Humboldt University before serving as Lehrstuhlinhaber at the University of Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Karttunen works in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He earned his BA at the University of Helsinki, studying under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola, among others. His career includes multiple research and teaching appointments at Helsinki and the Academy of Finland.

Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme at Frankfurt (1946–1954), and completed his Habilitation at Tübingen. He was an assistant at Göttingen (~1954–1957) and held a full professorship at Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Mylius was an Indologist who earned degrees at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig University. He held positions at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig University (1970–1991), the University of Bayreuth, and Goethe University Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and held a postdoctoral teaching staff appointment there in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn, a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, linguistic, and Buddhist studies, studied at Hamburg, Leipzig, and Giessen under scholars including Spuler, Lentz, and von Gabain. He held posts at Giessen and was Ordinarius for Turkology at Göttingen (1992–2003).
Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied under Paul Hacker. He held a post as Dozent at the University of Münster (attested 1978).

Klaus Wille is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with manuscript cataloguing at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997) and served as a research associate at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009, 2018–2026).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Marburg and habilitated at Hamburg under Michael Hahn and Klaus Sagaster. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and served as professor at the University of Vienna.

Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied theology at PTH Benediktbeuern (1966–1971), earned a doctorate in theology at the University of Munich (1978–1984), and served as a lecturer at Munich in 1996.

Klemens Karlsson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Schalk and received his Doctor of Philosophy from Uppsala University in 2000.

Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He received his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1989–1994) and served as a professor at the University of Bergen (1996) and the University of Oslo (~1996–1999).

Kobun Otogawa was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao, and Eihei-ji. He served at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center, Haiku Zendo (1970–1978), and taught regularly at Naropa University (2001).

Kodai Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple administrative and leadership positions at Komazawa University between 1892 and 1909 and lectured at the University of Tokyo.

Kodo Sawaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Koho Sawada, Sotan Oka, and Join Saeki at institutions including Horyuji Kangakuin. He served as professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).
Kodo Yamada was a scholar of Buddhist studies who held teaching posts at both Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University, studying under Shiro Matsumoto, and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.
Koen Wellens is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and earned a PhD at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst works in Indology, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1988–1992) and earned an MA from KU Leuven (completed by 1998).
